newsitem.title: USA: Mariachis, maids targeted in Texas border crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Mariachis, maids targeted in Texas border crackdown.

text.p: Mexican maids and mariachi musicians are the targets of a new crackdown on undocumented workers along the U.S.-Mexican border in Texas, officials said on Monday.

Law enforcement agencies raided five nightclubs in El Paso over the weekend and busted 20 mariachi players, who now await deportation hearings. Their employers face fines of up to $2,000 per undocumented worker.

"We are trying to return jobs to American workers," Dan Kane, a spokesman for the U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service, said. "Americans need to realise that they have to hire Americans even if they're just hiring someone to play music in their backyard for a wedding."

He said the INS plans to crack down on undocumented workers nationwide and that efforts on the southern border would focus largely on domestic maids and musicians, who typically live in Mexican border towns but cross over to the United States every day to go to work.
Undocumented Mexican women account for about 75 percent of all domestic help in El Paso and about half of the city's hugely popular mariachi musicians also work illegally.
"This kind of worksite enforcement will be a priority for us in '97," INS El Paso district director Luis Garcia said.
With unemployment running at 10-15 percent along the border, INS officials said more and more disgruntled U.S. citizens are reporting the use of undocumented workers.

But Kane said the problem reached much further than the border. He said large numbers of undocumented workers were employed, for example, in the motel-hotel industry in Albuquerque, in construction in Dallas, in Midwest meat-packing plants, in Delaware and Maryland chicken factories and in the New York garment industry.
"The further north you go, you find greater violations of immigration laws in the work place," Kane said.
